```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(infer)
library(randomForest)
library(tidymodels)
library(modelr)
library(yardstick)
```

Original Analysis:
```{r}
#load('data/biomarker-clean.RData')
#load('~/Desktop/Pstat 197A/module1-biomarker-main-team13/data/biomarker-clean.RData')

## MULTIPLE TESTING
####################

# function to compute tests
test_fn <- function(.df){
  t_test(.df, 
         formula = level ~ group,
         order = c('ASD', 'TD'),
         alternative = 'two-sided',
         var.equal = F)
}

ttests_out <- biomarker_clean %>%
  # drop ADOS score
  select(-ados) %>%
  # arrange in long format
  pivot_longer(-group, 
               names_to = 'protein', 
               values_to = 'level') %>%
  # nest by protein
  nest(data = c(level, group)) %>% 
  # compute t tests
  mutate(ttest = map(data, test_fn)) %>%
  unnest(ttest) %>%
  # sort by p-value
  arrange(p_value) %>%
  # multiple testing correction
  mutate(m = n(),
         hm = log(m) + 1/(2*m) - digamma(1),
         rank = row_number(),
         p.adj = m*hm*p_value/rank)

# select significant proteins
proteins_s1 <- ttests_out %>%
  slice_min(p.adj, n = 10) %>%
  pull(protein)

## RANDOM FOREST
##################

# store predictors and response separately
predictors <- biomarker_clean %>%
  select(-c(group, ados))

response <- biomarker_clean %>% pull(group) %>% factor()

# fit RF
set.seed(101422)
rf_out <- randomForest(x = predictors, 
                       y = response, 
                       ntree = 1000, 
                       importance = T)

# check errors
rf_out$confusion

# compute importance scores
proteins_s2 <- rf_out$importance %>% 
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(protein = rownames(rf_out$importance)) %>%
  slice_max(MeanDecreaseGini, n = 10) %>%
  pull(protein)

## LOGISTIC REGRESSION
#######################

# select subset of interest
proteins_sstar <- intersect(proteins_s1, proteins_s2)

biomarker_sstar <- biomarker_clean %>%
  select(group, any_of(proteins_sstar)) %>%
  mutate(class = (group == 'ASD')) %>%
  select(-group)

# partition into training and test set
set.seed(101422)
biomarker_split <- biomarker_sstar %>%
  initial_split(prop = 0.8)

# fit logistic regression model to training set
fit <- glm(class ~ ., 
           data = training(biomarker_split), 
           family = 'binomial')

# evaluate errors on test set
class_metrics <- metric_set(sensitivity, 
                            specificity, 
                            accuracy,
                            roc_auc)

og_results <- testing(biomarker_split) %>%
  add_predictions(fit, type = 'response') %>%
  mutate(class = factor(class),
    predicted_class = factor(pred > 0.5)
  ) %>%
  class_metrics(estimate = predicted_class,
                truth = class, pred,
                event_level = 'second'
  )

og_results
```
Original Results:
sensitivity: 0.9375000		
specificity: 0.7333333		
accuracy: 0.8387097		
roc_auc: 0.8958333	

Train/Test Split:
```{r}
set.seed(197)

subset <- sample(nrow(biomarker_clean), 110)

biomarker_train <- biomarker_clean[subset, ]

biomarker_test <- biomarker_clean[-subset, ]

ttests_out <- biomarker_train %>%
  select(-ados) %>%
  pivot_longer(-group, 
               names_to = 'protein', 
               values_to = 'level') %>%
  nest(data = c(level, group)) %>% 
  mutate(ttest = map(data, test_fn)) %>%
  unnest(ttest) %>%
  arrange(p_value) %>%
  mutate(m = n(),
         hm = log(m) + 1/(2*m) - digamma(1),
         rank = row_number(),
         p.adj = m*hm*p_value/rank)

proteins_s1 <- ttests_out %>%
  slice_min(p.adj, n = 10) %>%
  pull(protein)


predictors <- biomarker_train %>%
  select(-c(group, ados))

response <- biomarker_train %>% pull(group) %>% factor()

set.seed(101422)
rf_out <- randomForest(x = predictors, 
                       y = response, 
                       ntree = 1000, 
                       importance = T)

rf_out$confusion

proteins_s2 <- rf_out$importance %>% 
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(protein = rownames(rf_out$importance)) %>%
  slice_max(MeanDecreaseGini, n = 10) %>%
  pull(protein)


proteins_sstar <- intersect(proteins_s1, proteins_s2)

sstar <- function(df) {df %>%
  select(group, any_of(proteins_sstar)) %>%
  mutate(class = (group == 'ASD')) %>%
  select(-group)}

training_sstar <- sstar(biomarker_train)
testing_sstar <- sstar(biomarker_test)

fit <- glm(class ~ ., 
           data = training_sstar, 
           family = 'binomial')

class_metrics <- metric_set(sensitivity, 
                            specificity, 
                            accuracy,
                            roc_auc)


train_results <- testing_sstar %>%
  add_predictions(fit, type = 'response') %>%
  mutate(class = factor(class),
    predicted_class = factor(pred > 0.5)
  ) %>%
  class_metrics(estimate = predicted_class,
                truth = class, pred,
                event_level = 'second'
  )

print(train_results)

data.frame(metric = og_results$.metric, 
           diff =  train_results$.estimate - og_results$.estimate)

# When we carry out the entire selection procedure on a training partition
# Every estimated value is significantly lower than our initial findings
# The smallest metric difference, specificity, is a decrease of approximately .09
# The largest metric decrease, sensitivity, is by approximately 0.33
# Overall, our new model performs worst than our original analysis
# However, it is important to note that our original analysis may have overfitted
# Note that our diff column is (new - old)
```
Train/Test Split Results:
sensitivity: 0.545
specificity: 0.636
accuracy: 0.591
roc_auc: 0.705

Fuzzy Intersection:
```{r}
set.seed(101422)

#Assigning protein membership score by min-max normalization

# Rank all proteins by RF importance
rf_membership <- rf_out$importance %>%
  as_tibble(rownames = "protein") %>%
  mutate(
    rf_rank = rank(-MeanDecreaseGini),
    mu_rf = 1 - (rf_rank - 1) / (n() - 1)
  ) %>%
  select(protein, rf_rank, mu_rf)

# Rank all proteins by adjusted t-test p-value
t_membership <- ttests_out %>%
  mutate(
    t_rank = rank(p.adj),
    mu_t = 1 - (t_rank - 1) / (n() - 1)
  ) %>%
  select(protein, t_rank, mu_t)

# Combine memberships using the minimum operator
fuzzy_proteins <- inner_join(
  rf_membership, t_membership,
  by = "protein"
) %>%
  mutate(
    mu_fuzzy = pmin(mu_rf, mu_t)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mu_fuzzy))

# Select the proteins with the highest fuzzy memberships
proteins_fuzzy <- fuzzy_proteins %>%
  slice_max(mu_fuzzy, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  pull(protein)
```

```{r}
setdiff(proteins_fuzzy, proteins_sstar)
setdiff(proteins_sstar, proteins_fuzzy)
```

Logistic Regression
```{r}
biomarker_fuzzy <- biomarker_clean %>%
  select(group, any_of(proteins_fuzzy)) %>%
  mutate(class = (group == 'ASD')) %>%
  select(-group)

# partition into training and test set
set.seed(101422)
biomarker_split <- biomarker_fuzzy %>%
  initial_split(prop = 0.8)

# fit logistic regression model to training set
fit <- glm(class ~ ., 
           data = training(biomarker_split), 
           family = 'binomial')

# evaluate errors on test set
class_metrics <- metric_set(sensitivity, 
                            specificity, 
                            accuracy,
                            roc_auc)

fuzzy_results <- testing(biomarker_split) %>%
  add_predictions(fit, type = 'response') %>%
  mutate(class = factor(class),
    predicted_class = factor(pred > 0.5)
  ) %>%
  class_metrics(estimate = predicted_class,
                truth = class, pred,
                event_level = 'second'
  )

data.frame(metric = og_results$.metric, 
           diff = fuzzy_results$.estimate - og_results$.estimate)

#Through fuzzy intersection, we achieved a raw overall improvement
#Specificity (0.2) and auc (0.05), slight decrease in sensitivity (-0.19)
#Applied min-max normalization to calculate membership of rf and t-test, which we took the pmin between the two membership scores.
#Should account for different methods in calculating membership scores.
```
